yuri 0.3-9
  • Reference

    Get a data set

    dataURI.Rd

    Download the files associated with a URI and return the filenames.

    dataURI(uri, path, cache=TRUE, unzip=TRUE, filter=TRUE, authentication=NULL, keep_folders=TRUE)

    Arguments

    uri

    character. The URI of a dataset

    path

    character. The path to where the data should be saved. The simplified uri is always appended to this path

    cache

    logical. if TRUE the data are only downloaded again if they are not locally available

    unzip

    logical. if TRUE downloaded zip files are unzipped

    filter

    logical. if TRUE files that probably do not have the primary data are filtered out (files ending on .pdf, .doc(x), .json)

    authentication

    optional named list of credentials for the data provider. May be a flat list of fields for the URI's provider (e.g. list(token = "...", email = "...")), or a service-keyed list like authenticate (e.g. list(DATAVERSE = list(token = "..."), DRYAD = list(username = "...", password = "..."))). Recognized fields depend on the provider (see Details). If NULL, credentials registered via authenticate and environment variables are used.

    keep_folders

    logical. if TRUE (default) and unzip=TRUE, preserve the directory structure inside zip archives. If FALSE, files are extracted into a flat folder (equivalent to utils::unzip(..., junkpaths=TRUE)). The returned file list always includes files in sub-directories.

    Details

    Some Harvard Dataverse (and other Dataverse) datasets require a guestbook before bulk file download. In that case, dataURI POSTs to the Dataverse Access API with signed=true and a guestbook payload, then downloads via the returned signed URL (see the Data Access API guide).

    Credential resolution order is: fields in authentication, then credentials registered via authenticate, then environment variables (YURI_DATAVERSE_* and the historical DATAVERSE_GUESTBOOK_*), then built-in defaults.

    For Dataverse, recognized authentication fields include name (or username), email, institution (or institute), token (or api_token / password), position, and answers. Register persistent credentials with authenticate(list(DATAVERSE = list(name, email, institution, position, token, answers))) (use GET /api/guestbooks/{id} to inspect what the server asks for).

    For Dryad, recognized fields are username (or client_id) and password (or client_secret / secret) — the OAuth client id and secret.

    Custom guestbook questions must be supplied in answers as a list of lists with id and value elements (see Dataverse API examples).

    Value

    character, the downloaded file names
